headline: US electronics factory-gate prices climb 12% as Bulgarian mining halves
text:
# US electronics factory-gate prices climb 12% as Bulgarian mining halves

## Today in the data

The single largest departure from habit in a monthly series this morning is American. The BLS producer price index for computer and electronic products, held in **us-ppi-sectors** as `computer_electronic`, stood at 118.276 in July 2026, against 105.303 in July 2025 — up 12.3% on the year, where the usual twelve-month change in this series since it starts in December 2004 is +0.57%. This is not a one-month jump: the monthly path I pulled shows 108.234 in December 2025, 112.659 in January 2026, 115.699 in March and 118.043 in April, so most of the rise was booked in the first four months of the year and the index has been flat since (117.878 in May, 118.306 in June, 118.276 in July). A sector whose factory-gate prices normally fall or crawl has repriced by an eighth in twelve months.

What usually accompanies such a move in this collection is a volume story, and here it does not line up neatly. In **us-chips**, Federal Reserve industrial production for semiconductors and other electronic components reached 191.9 (2017 = 100) in July 2026 and the broader electronics line 140.6, both at or near the top of their range. Rising prices and rising output together point to demand rather than to a supply squeeze, but the caveat on that dataset matters: the Fed quality-adjusts the semiconductor index, so it rises with chip performance and not only with units shipped. Worth checking against the September release of us-ppi-sectors and us-ip-sectors, both of which last print July 2026.

The second cluster is European electricity retail. In **energy-household-eu**, Austria paid 0.3272 euro per kWh in the second half of 2025, all taxes included, up 34.3% from 0.2437 in H2 2024 — the biggest year-on-year rise in a record beginning in 2008, against a usual +2.58%. The series I pulled shows why the base matters: Austria was at 0.2731 in H1 2024 and then dropped to 0.2437 in H2 2024, so a large part of the 34% is the year-earlier dip unwinding, with the level in H2 2025 still only about 20% above H1 2024. Luxembourg tells a similar story with a cleaner base, moving from 0.2024 in H2 2024 to 0.2665 in H2 2025, +31.7%, its own record. These are half-yearly, tax-inclusive figures in euro, so a change in a levy or the removal of a subsidy shows up as a price move; that is a hypothesis for the next Eurostat vintage rather than a reading from the number.

Bulgaria's mining index is the sharpest fall among monthly series. **eu-mining-ipi** puts `BG|B`, mining and quarrying, at 50.3 in June 2026 (2021 = 100) against 97.3 in June 2025, down 48.3% — the steepest twelve-month fall since the record starts in January 2001. The monthly path rules out a single bad month: 81.9 in December 2025, 66.5 in January, 61.4 in March, 55.7 in April, 56.4 in May, 50.3 in June. That is a six-month slide, in a seasonally and calendar-adjusted volume index, that has taken output to roughly half the 2021 average. The base month is also unhelpful — 97.3 was the highest print in the past year — so the headline percentage overstates the trend break somewhat while the level does not.

Two annual moves belong to the same energy transition. In **electricity-mix**, UK coal generation was 0.33 TWh in 2025 against 1.90 TWh in 2024, down 82.6% in a record that starts in 1921. In absolute terms this is now a rounding error in a system of hundreds of terawatt-hours; the interesting fact is that it is 0.33 and not zero, and the dataset's own caveat says the last year is often Ember's provisional figure. Alongside it, **eu-renewables-share** has Greece's electricity share at 60.9% of gross final consumption in 2025, up 9.65 points from 51.248% in 2024 and up from 35.9% in 2020 — the biggest one-year gain since 2005, against a usual +2.17 points. These are Renewable Energy Directive accounting figures, not Ember generation shares, so they are not interchangeable with the coal number.

Three smaller items deserve a line each rather than a paragraph. **macro-external** shows Egypt's net FDI inflow at 15.5bn current US dollars in 2025 after 46.6bn in 2024, a fall of 31.1bn; the 2024 figure was itself an outlier in a series running from 1971, so this is a return from an exceptional year, not a collapse from trend. **eu-car-registrations** has Estonia's diesel registrations at 1,738 cars in 2025, down 70.4%, with the total at 13,141, down 49% — but the record only starts in 2014 and the counts are small, so a tax change or a pull-forward of purchases into 2024 would move these percentages easily. And **eu-vet-weight** puts Belgium's veterinary and pet-services weight at 3.63 per mille of the basket in 2025 against 2.56 in 2024: a 41.8% rise in a weight that is barely a third of one percent of spending.

## Charts

[US electronics factory-gate prices and semiconductor output](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Look at the price line's step change from December 2025 to April 2026 and ask whether the output lines (right axis) bend at the same time.

[Household electricity bills: Austria and Luxembourg, EUR per kWh](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Watch the Austrian dip in H2 2024 that flatters this year's percentage, and Luxembourg's flat 2010s before the 2025 step.

[Bulgarian mining output, 2021 = 100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The point is the level, not the percentage: whether 50.3 in June 2026 is below anything in the previous decade of this series.

## Numbers desk

### Forecasts

For **us-ppi-sectors** `computer_electronic`, the last observation is 118.276 in July 2026. The tool chose Holt-Winters additive with period 12 and projects 120.35 for October 2026, with a 95% band of 118.93 to 121.76 — the band is the residual spread grown at the random-walk rate, so it says where the series would land if the last year's drift continued and nothing else changed. In-sample MAPE is 0.27%, which reflects a smooth index rather than any forecasting skill on a turning point.

For **eu-mining-ipi** `BG|B`, the last observation is 50.3 in June 2026. Holt-Winters additive, period 12, projects 62.99 for September 2026 with a band of 32.35 to 93.64. That band is wider than the level itself is informative: the method's seasonal terms pull the projection back up while the trend term is negative (−0.37 per month), and the residual standard deviation is 9.03 index points. Read it as an admission that the past six months carry almost no information about September.

For **energy-household-eu** `AT`, the last observation is 0.3272 euro per kWh in H2 2025. Holt-Winters additive, period 2, projects 0.3249 for H2 2026 with a band of 0.2904 to 0.3594. This is a projection of the series' own past and nothing more: household tariffs of this kind are set with taxes, levies and regulated components, so the number should be read as arithmetic on history, not as a price expectation.

### Correlations

Austria against Luxembourg in **energy-household-eu**, 2010-S1 to 2025-S2, 32 shared half-years: the levels correlation is 0.904 but both series trend, so that figure carries no information about co-movement. On year-on-year changes, r = 0.534 across 30 observations — the two national bills do move together, consistent with a shared euro-area wholesale market and a common policy calendar, though with only 30 half-yearly points this is a modest reading and the tool offers no band for it.

US electronics prices against US semiconductor output — `computer_electronic` in **us-ppi-sectors** against `semiconductors_ip` in **us-chips**, both year-on-year, January 2010 to July 2026, 199 months: the strongest correlation is r = −0.262 at lag −3, with output leading. The tool's Bartlett band, widened to 0.449 because both series repeat themselves, is not cleared at any lag from −12 to +12. Not distinguishable from zero. The price rise and the output level are, on this evidence, separate facts.

## What to watch

- **us-ppi-sectors** and **us-ip-sectors**, both last at July 2026: whether the electronics price index resumes the January-to-April climb or stays on the plateau it has held since May, and whether the output side moves with it.
- **eu-mining-ipi**, last at July 2026 for the dataset as a whole and June 2026 for Bulgaria: one more print settles whether 50.3 is a floor or a waypoint, and the Holt-Winters projection of 57 to 63 is the number to judge it against.
- **us-chips**, last at July 2026: the semiconductor and electronics production indices are the volume check on the price story, subject to the Fed's quality adjustment.
- **cpi-eu** and **eu-hicp**, both last at July 2026: whether household energy prices of the kind Eurostat's nrg_pc_204 records in Austria and Luxembourg are showing up in the consumer indices.
- **vet-cpi-eu** and **eu-vet-weight** (the CPI file last at December 2025): whether Belgium's jump in basket weight is matched by a price move, or is a reweighting artefact.

## Sources

Eurostat nrg_pc_204, electricity prices for household consumers, band DC, all taxes and levies included, euro per kWh, semi-annual — **energy-household-eu**, last observation 2025-S2.
BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly — **us-ppi-sectors**, last observation 2026-07.
Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED, monthly, seasonally adjusted, NAICS 3344 and 334 — **us-chips**, last observation 2026-07.
Eurostat sts_inpr_m, production in industry, seasonally and calendar adjusted, 2021 = 100, monthly — **eu-mining-ipi**, last observation 2026-06 for BG|B.
Ember Yearly Electricity Data and the Energy Institute Statistical Review via Our World in Data, TWh, annual — **electricity-mix**, last observation 2025.
Eurostat nrg_ind_ren, share of energy from renewable sources, annual — **eu-renewables-share**, last observation 2025.
World Bank World Development Indicators, external accounts and FDI, 30 economies — **macro-external**, last observation 2025 (quoted from the context note, not re-pulled).
Eurostat road_eqr_carpda, new passenger car registrations by motor energy, annual — **eu-car-registrations**, last observation 2025 (quoted from the context note, not re-pulled).
Eurostat HICP item weights, veterinary and pet services — **eu-vet-weight**, last observation 2025 (quoted from the context note, not re-pulled).
